_about: Launch radar sources: official feeds and pages only for launches (no news sites, no rumours). Sources with role 'trending' (Techmeme, Google News) are news aggregators for the news page's trending tier only (radar/trending.mjs: Techmeme top headlines or 3+ reputable outlets, allowed topics, safety filter, 4 a day); 'outlet' names a reputable outlet whose feed counts toward that rule. Indian outlets (ET, Mint, Business Standard, The Hindu/BusinessLine, HT, Indian Express, Moneycontrol, NDTV, MediaNama, Inc42, AIM, YourStory) count toward the 3-outlet rule since 19 Nov 2026, but none of their own feeds permits commercial use (checked 2026-11-19, see notUsed), so Indian stories reach the tier only through Techmeme or Google News grouping. Sources with category 'incident' are security news and vendor security blogs, used only to discover incidents (scoreIncident in lib.mjs) and service outages on major platforms (scoreOutage); the writer cites primary sources and labels claims (site automation/RADAR.md). Sources with category 'outage' are official status pages: only open, large incidents qualify (impact and component gates: minImpact, minComponents, minComponentsCritical, assumeMajor), never scheduled maintenance, and resolved ones can only update an existing outage guide; allowEmpty = an empty feed is normal (no incident). 'verified' = HTTP 200 with parseable items from an honest user agent on that date. Weight shifts every item's score for that source (high-volume or broad feeds get 0 or less). categoryBoost adds points per feed category; '(none)' applies when an item has no category.

sources.name: Microsoft 365 Message Center (community mirror mc.merill.net)
sources.note: Message Center is where retirements and changes are announced; pubDate is the last update. Low weight so routine rollouts stay below the threshold; M365 retirements due within 120 days clear it through the retirement floor in lib.mjs. Cite the MC number and confirm on Microsoft Learn.

sources.name: Tech Community: Windows IT Pro Blog
Anthropic News
sources.note: Since autumn 2026 this page carries mostly company news (IPO, policy, partnerships); Claude product launches are posted on claude.com (claude-articles).

sources.name: Claude by Anthropic: articles (product updates)
sources.note: Where Claude launches are announced (e.g. Claude for Manufacturing on 12 Nov 2026, which never appeared on anthropic.com/news). Cards carry the date as text ('Nov 12, 2026') and the summary inside the link; no RSS (rss.xml 404) and the sitemap has no dates; claude.com/blog redirects here. detail: true = the article page of each new, fresh item is read for scoring (settings.detailPerSource).

sources.name: Reserve Bank of India press releases
Shopify Changelog
sources.note: High-volume merchant changelog (about 1,600 items in the feed): 3 a day at most on the news page. shopify.com/news/feed is stale (last item 2023).

sources.name: AWS What's New
sources.note: About 100 items, dozens a day (including Amazon Bedrock and Nova model launches). Low weight and briefMax 6: only the clearest launches and model news reach the news page.

sources.name: Azure Updates
sources.note: About 200 items incl. "Retirement:" notices (Azure OpenAI model retirements arrive here). A retirement of an AI model businesses use clears the Tier-1 floor when due within 120 days (brief.mjs tier1Floor).

sources.name: Gemini API release notes
sources.note: Redirects to aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog; the page carries its Markdown ("## November 12, 2026" + bullets) in a <noscript> block. New models, GA, pricing and deprecations.

sources.name: Meta Newsroom: AI (Llama, Meta AI)
sources.note: ai.meta.com/blog renders with JavaScript and has no feed; Llama and Meta AI launches are posted on the Newsroom AI tag (overlaps meta-newsroom; merged by link).

sources.name: Microsoft AI (MAI) news (sitemap)
sources.note: MAI model news (MAI-Image, MAI-Voice). Title from the URL slug, date = sitemap lastmod; the article page description is read for the news page.

sources.name: AWS Machine Learning Blog
sources.note: Mostly customer stories; kept for Bedrock and Nova model posts (AI model detection), at most 2 a day.

sources.name: ElevenLabs Blog
sources.note: Many explainer posts (NOISE in brief.mjs drops guides); model launches pass.

sources.name: Hugging Face trending (official lab accounts)
sources.label: Model card published on Hugging Face by the vendor account (trending signal, not an announcement).
sources.note: Signal only (role signal): never a fast-track article. Kept only for the official lab accounts in orgs; date = repository creation. Covers Qwen and DeepSeek, whose own sites have no dated feed.

sources.name: Intel Newsroom
sources.note: newsroom.intel.com/feed now redirects to this HTML page (no feed); cards carry dates.

sources.name: Qualcomm press releases (sitemap)
sources.note: About 1.7 MB; no feed (news/rss 404, investor RSS 403). Title from the slug, date = lastmod; the release page description is read for the news page.

sources.name: Samsung Newsroom India
sources.note: India launch prices and availability for Galaxy devices.

sources.name: Dell Technologies Blog
sources.note: Mixes launches with evergreen how-to posts (NOISE in brief.mjs drops those).

sources.name: GSMArena news
sources.note: Headlines only, as a launch signal; never a source of device specs (the device portal uses manufacturer pages only).

sources.name: Techmeme (top headlines)
sources.note: Techmeme's top headlines (about 15 items). A story listed here qualifies for the news page's trending tier (radar/trending.mjs) when it is on an allowed topic and passes the safety filter. The item links the original outlet's article (gift tokens stripped), never Techmeme. Discovery only: never a fast-track article, except a clearly-IT outage, scored by the existing outage logic (outageWeight).

sources.name: Google News: Technology (US)
sources.note: Redirects (302) to the topics/CAAq... feed; about 70 items, each with the other outlets Google grouped with it (counted for the 3-reputable-outlets rule). Mostly consumer and gaming news, which the allowed topics filter out. Links are news.google.com redirects; a direct outlet link (Techmeme, The Verge, ...) is preferred when the story has one. Google says the feed is for feed readers, so it is used for discovery only: the page writes its own neutral lines and links the outlet.

sources.name: Google News search: leadership changes at major tech companies
sources.note: Search feed (last day, about 100 items, ranked by relevance, not date) for CEO changes at the companies in radar/trending.mjs COMPANIES. Much commentary and scandal coverage: the allowed-topic, opinion and safety filters keep only the neutral fact, and only when 3+ reputable outlets or Techmeme carry it. One long query mixing all topics had poor recall (tested 2026-11-15), hence one feed per topic.

sources.name: Google News search: IPOs and valuations of major tech companies
sources.note: Search feed (last day). Small-startup funding rounds, stock moves and investor commentary are filtered out in trending.mjs; only IPO and valuation news of the listed companies qualifies.

sources.name: Google News search: space and EV milestones
sources.note: Search feed (last day) for rocket launches, landings and catches and for robotaxi / EV launches and orders. Product and AI model milestones of the other companies come through Techmeme and the Google News Technology topic.

sources.name: Google News search: critical-infrastructure outages
sources.note: Search feed (last day) for ground stops and nationwide airline, bank, payment, 911 and network outages. Non-IT outages are Tier 2 only (trending tier, kind outage); an outage of a platform the outage guides cover (lib.mjs OUTAGE_PLATFORMS) goes through the existing outage logic.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.note: Security news: discovery only. The writer cites the primary source (vendor or company statement, researcher post, exchange filing, advisory) and labels unverified claims.

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.note: All-news feed (not security-only; e.g. /news/microsoft/ stories arrive with category 'Microsoft'). Security news and service outages: discovery only (see thn). Outage wording on a major platform is scored by scoreOutage; only the Gaming/Deals category penalties apply there.

sources.name: GitHub Blog: Security
sources.note: Official GitHub security posts and advisories (also feature posts; those are rejected unless they describe an incident or vulnerability with a user action).

sources.name: Microsoft Security Blog
sources.note: Official Microsoft threat intelligence and incident posts. Stands in for the MSRC blog, which has no working feed (see notUsed).

sources.name: ThePrint: Tech
sources.note: Indian tech and business news, for Indian bank, UPI, Aadhaar and consumer breaches. Discovery only: cite the company's exchange filing or statement first. TERMS (checked 2026-11-19, owner to decide): robots.txt allows the feed, but ThePrint's terms of use (theprint.in/terms-of-use) permit only non-commercial personal use and forbid commercial use of its content.

sources.name: MediaNama
sources.note: Indian tech policy news, for Indian consumer breaches and CERT-In or RBI actions. Discovery only (see theprint-tech). TERMS (checked 2026-11-19, owner to decide): MediaNama's robots.txt has 'Disallow: */feed/*' for all user agents, and its terms (medianama.com/terms-of-use, sections 7-8) forbid using RSS content beyond personal, non-commercial use, automated collection, and putting its content into any AI model. Not given an 'outlet' for the trending tier for that reason.

sources.name: Fortinet Threat Research
sources.note: Vendor threat research: discovery only, scored as security news (scoreIncident).

sources.name: Microsoft 365 status (status.cloud.microsoft, admin center post)
sources.note: Public, no auth. Microsoft posts here only when a broad Microsoft 365 incident stops admins from reading Service health; Status 'Available' = no incident (no items). Tenant Service health (incident IDs such as EX1550543) needs Graph auth and is not used.

sources.name: Microsoft 365 consumer status (status.cloud.microsoft)
sources.note: Public, no auth. Outlook.com, OneDrive, Teams (free) and Microsoft 365 consumer incidents; services listed as 'Operational' are skipped.

sources.name: Azure status RSS
sources.note: Lists only active broad-impact Azure incidents (narrower ones go to each subscription's Service Health), so an empty channel is normal. Status/impact come from the item wording.

sources.name: Google Workspace Status Dashboard (incidents.json)
sources.note: About 280 KB, full history with severity (high = critical, medium = major) and affected products. Qualifies: high severity on 2+ products or on Gmail/Drive/Meet/Docs/Calendar/Chat, or medium on 2+ products. The Atom feed (dashboard/en/feed.atom) carries only the latest update and no severity.

sources.name: Google Cloud Service Health (incidents.json)
sources.note: About 290 KB. Qualifies: high severity, or medium on 5+ products or 3+ regions (single-product regional issues stay out).

sources.name: GitHub Status (Statuspage incidents.json)
sources.note: About 300 KB, last 50 incidents with impact and components. GitHub marks several incidents a week major or critical, so only 4+ components (or 'multiple services' wording) qualify. history.rss has no impact field.

sources.name: Cloudflare Status (Statuspage incidents.json)
sources.note: About 120 KB. Scheduled maintenance is a separate endpoint, so none of it appears here; single-PoP components ('City, Country - (XXX)') are not counted. history.rss is not used: its 25 items are almost all per-city scheduled maintenance.

sources.name: AWS Health Dashboard RSS (all services)
sources.note: About 70 KB; one item per service and region, every item linking to the same page (anchorFromGuid keeps them apart). A single service in one region never qualifies; 'Multiple services' events or multi-service/multi-region wording do. Titles prefixed 'Service is operating normally' / [RESOLVED] are resolved.
